facts.raw_span: a two-week history of an asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face
reduced mouth opening
two prior similar episodes over eight years
no pain or fever
a known diabetic on regular medication
gross right facial asymmetry
a 6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling
the borders were ill-defined, the consistency ranged from soft to firm
no lymphadenopathy, paresthesia, or facial palsy
Contrast-enhanced CT of the face showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space
Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content were noted, and there was erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla
a clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement

concepts.why: The patient has a two-week history of an asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face, with a previous diagnosis of a buccal-space infection and a current clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement.
The patient is a known diabetic and has gross right facial asymmetry, which could be related to diabetic cheilitis.
The contrast-enhanced CT of the face showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space, which could be a buccal space cyst.
The patient has reduced mouth opening and a subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders, which could be related to necrotizing sialometaplasia.
The patient has a history of asymptomatic swelling and a clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess, which could be caused by Staphylococcus.
The patient has a history of recurrent episodes of swelling and a subcutaneous mass with cystic areas, which could be related to actinomycosis.
The patient has gross right facial asymmetry and a subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders, which could be related to squamous cell carcinoma.
The patient has a subcutaneous swelling with cystic areas and no lymphadenopathy, which could be related to a mucocele.

rationales.F01: Asymptomatic swelling in the right lower half of the face is consistent with a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F07: A 6 × 6 cm ovoid subcutaneous swelling with ill-defined borders and variable consistency is suggestive of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F10: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a well-defined soft-tissue mass with cystic areas in the right buccal space supports the diagnosis of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F11: Intracystic loculations with dense cystic content and erosion of the posterior buccal cortex without perforation of the maxilla are characteristic of a chronic buccal space abscess.
rationales.F12: A clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement is consistent with the patient's presentation and imaging findings.
